# List of natural monuments of the United Kingdom

The United Kingdom does not use the term “natural monument” as a statutory conservation designation. It does not apply the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Category III (Natural Monument or Feature) classification in domestic law or in its system of protected areas.
Globally, however, a natural monument typically refers to a single natural feature of outstanding scientific, cultural, or scenic value. In many countries — particularly in parts of Europe, Asia, and Latin America — the term is used as a formal legal designation corresponding to IUCN Category III.
Instead, in the UK, individual natural features of scientific or scenic importance are protected under other designations, most commonly as Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs) under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, as well as through National Nature Reserves, Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty, and ownership by conservation bodies such as the National Trust.
A natural monument is distinct from a prehistoric human-made monument such as Stonehenge. The UK also has scheduled monuments, which are nationally important archaeological sites.
The following is a non-exhaustive list.
Geological and geomorphological features
* White Cliffs of Dover
* Brimham Rocks
* Cheddar Gorge
* Durdle Door (coastal rock formation)
* Giant's Causeway (basalt columns)
* The Trinnacle (rock formation)
* High Force (waterfall)
* Jurassic Coast
* Malham Cove (rock formation)
* Old Man of Hoy (sea stack)
* Pistyll Rhaeadr (waterfall)
* The Needles (chalk formation)
* The Storr (rock formation)
